AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the administrative code of the
city of New York, in relation to requiring background checks for for-hire

items.lawCode: Add Art 17-D §499-m, V & T L; amd §19-504, NYC Ad Cd
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6190

SPONSOR: MARTINEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the
administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring
background checks for for-hire vehicle licenses

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill ensures the safety of all New Yorkers by requiring a thorough
state and federal background check for all operators of for-hire vehi-
cles.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

The vehicle and traffic law is amended by adding a new article 17-C
which would require prior to the issuance of a taxicab, limousine,
commuter van, paratransit or for-hire vehicle license, the applicant for
such license be fingerprinted by the licensing authority authorized to
issue such license for the purpose of securing criminal history records
from both the state division of criminal justice services and the feder-
al bureau of investigation.

Subdivision 1 of section 19-504 of the administrative code of the city
of New York, as added by local law number 115 of the city of New York
for the year 1993, is amended and a new subdivision q is added to
require fingerprinting by the licensing authority to secure criminal
history records by both the state division of criminal justice services
and the federal bureau of investigation.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Since the tragic events of September 11th the security of our citizens,
financial institutions and landmarks have gained increased importance.
With the threat of terrorism becoming a regular occurrence measures must
be taken to ensure that proper precautions are taken to guarantee the
utmost safety of all New Yorkers. With relatively easy access to most
buildings, limousines and other forms of for-hire vehicles have become
an increasingly popular weapon for terrorists. The size of the vehicles
combined with their accessibility to targets make them perfect for car
bombings by terrorist and extremist groups.

Currently operators of these vehicles are subject only to state criminal
background checks leaving out any offenses perpetrated outside of New
York or the United States. During this time of heightened threat to the
safety of our nation, security loopholes such as this must be closed.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2004: A11838 Referred to Transportation 2005/06: Referred to Transporta-
tion
2007/08: A689 Referred to Transportation
2009/10: A6395 Referred to Transportation
2011/12: A1147 Held in Transportation
2013/14: A2879 Referred to Transportation
2015/16: A8418 Referred to Transportation
2017/18: A3425 Referred to Transportation

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:
None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6190A

SPONSOR: MARTINEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the
administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring
background checks for for-hire vehicle driver or owner licenses

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL::

This bill ensures the safety of all New Yorkers by requiring a thorough
state and federal background check for all operators of for-hire vehi-
cles.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS::

The vehicle and traffic law is amended by adding a new article 17-C
which would require prior to the issuance of a taxicab, limousine,
commuter van, paratransit or for-hire vehicle license, the applicant for
such license be fingerprinted by the licensing authority authorized to
issue such license for the purpose of securing criminal history records
from both the state division of criminal justice services and the feder-
al bureau of investigation.

Subdivision 1 of section 19-504 of the administrative code of the city
of New York, as added by local law number 115 of the city of New York
for the year 1993, is amended and a new subdivision q is added to
require fingerprinting by the licensing authority to secure criminal
history records by both the state division of criminal justice services
and the federal bureau of investigation.

 
JUSTIFICATION::

Under current law, employers of bus drivers must conduct a background
investigation of a new driver's employment history for the past three
years, and obtain driving records for the driver for the past three
years. School bus driver employers must request a criminal history check
of each driver based on his/her fingerprints. To obtain a hazardous
materials commercial driver's license (CDL), an applicant is subjected
to fingerprinting and a background check and security threat check.

However, the Suffolk County special grand jury impaneled after a stretch
limousine crash in Cutchogue noted that the Department of Motor Vehicles
(DMV) does not require background checks or fingerprinting for taxi and
limousine and other for-hire vehicle drivers, and that such requirements
are currently dependent on local taxi and limousine commissions.

This legislation seeks to treat for-hire vehicles (FHVs) similarly to
other motor carriers and close potential gaps, subjecting prospective
FHV drivers to fingerprinting and criminal history checks by both the
Division of, Criminal Justice Services (DCJS) and Federal Bureau of
Investigation (FBI).
